I added the integration test at `services/notifier/tests/test_email_integration.py`, but it hasn't sent a real email yet. When I ran it, it skipped because no sandbox credentials are set in this environment. So it is unverified, and the part that checks delivery is partly a guess (details below).

**What the test does:**
- It sends one real receipt through `provider.send` to `receipts@sink.acme.test`. The sandbox returns 202 for any recipient but only actually delivers to `@sink.acme.test`, so a delivery check sent anywhere else would never pass.
- It then checks the sink inbox every 2s, for up to 60s, for a message with the id the provider returned. Once found, it checks the recipient, subject, and that the body contains a unique invoice id.
- It sends exactly one message per run, because the sandbox is limited to 2 messages a second and 500 a day for the whole team.
- It's marked `integration`, so `make test-fast` leaves it out. It skips unless both `MAIL_API_KEY` (the sandbox key) and `MAIL_SINK_URL` are set.

**Things you should know:**
1. **`render()` isn't written yet.** It raises `NotImplementedError`, so `send_receipt()` can't run end to end. The test replaces only `render` with a fixed HTML body; the call to the provider is real. Once `render` exists, delete that stub and the test covers the real template too.
2. **I guessed how the sink inbox API works.** Nothing in the repo describes it, so I assumed `GET {MAIL_SINK_URL}/messages?to=...` with the same bearer token, returning `{"messages": [{"id", "to", "subject", "html"}]}`. Please check this against the provider's sink docs; `_wait_for_message` is the only part to change.

**To run it:**
```
cd services/notifier
MAIL_API_KEY=<sandbox key> MAIL_SINK_URL=<sink base url> python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests -m integration
```
The existing unit test still passes.
